title: Geometric signatures of the onset of many-body ergodicity
authors: Chris Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, Francisco Machado, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ
abstract: Identifying universal, robust, and interpretable signatures of the onset of ergodicity remains a major challenge. The adiabatic gauge potential has been noted to act as a sensitive probe of quantum chaos. In this work, we generalize the features of the adiabatic gauge potential to multi-parameter perturbations, yielding an emergent quantum geometry. We dub this geometry the Hilbert-Killing metric, which allows us to study the onset of ergodicity in many-body quantum systems. Our Hilbert-Killing metric sensitively probes the boundary between ergodic and integrable regimes across all investigated geometric components. This boundary is uniquely identified by the presence of the consistently fastest growth with system size, which is corroborated by extensive numerical investigations of the Ising and PXP models.
summary: The paper introduces the Hilbert-Killing metric, an emergent quantum geometry derived from generalizing the adiabatic gauge potential. This metric serves as a sensitive diagnostic tool to locate the boundary between integrable and ergodic regimes in many-body quantum systems like the Ising model. Its robust scaling behavior at this phase transition makes it a powerful theoretical signature for studying quantum thermalization.
main_problem: The central challenge is finding universal, robust, and interpretable geometric signatures that mark the precise onset of many-body ergodicity in quantum systems.
main_result: The derived Hilbert-Killing (HK) metric successfully probes this boundary, showing its maximum response precisely where the system transitions between integrable and ergodic regimes for both Ising and PXP models.
method: The authors generalize the adiabatic gauge potential to multi-parameter perturbations, constructing the HK metric tensor which quantifies total eigenstate variation across parameter space.
model_or_system: The study uses general quantum many-body systems, specifically analyzing the spin-1/2 one-dimensional mixed field Ising model and a constrained PXP model, parameterized by external fields ($h_x, h_z$).
key_observables:
Hilbert-Killing (HK) metric components ($G_{\mu
u}$), spectrum-averaged variance of the AGP ($\sigma^2_{A_\mu}$), and the Casimir invariant ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: The system parameters defining the Hamiltonian, particularly investigating the crossover region between integrable and ergodic limits.
main_assumptions: Previous metrics are often ill-behaved near the boundary; the HK metric is proposed to overcome this by providing a comprehensive geometric measure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept of the HK metric defining geometry in parameter space, showing maximum scaling response at the ergodic/integrable phase boundary for both Ising and PXP models.
paper_structure: The paper develops the HK metric from the adiabatic gauge potential, applies it to analyze the Ising model across different phases (Fig. 1, 2), confirms universality using the PXP model (Fig. 3), and explores deeper connections via entanglement fidelity and Casimir invariants in random matrix models (Fig. 4-8).
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful geometric tool to diagnose thermalization dynamics, which is crucial for understanding quantum chaos and non-equilibrium steady states relevant to AMO physics.
